title: Making 100
objectives: Find the complement of a number to 100 in one step
Subtract by counting up the gap instead of borrowing

screens.title: Making 100
screens.prose: Change from a £100 note, the gap between two prices, the distance to a target. Each is a subtraction you can do by counting up.
Here is a number line from 30 to 100. One point sits at 37 and the other at 100.
screens.question: How far is it from 37 up to 100?

hints.text: Hop to the next ten first.
40 to 100 is 60, so the gap is $3 + 60 = 63$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 37: first to 40, then to 100.

byKey.ten-each: You took each digit up to 10: 3 to 7 and 7 to 3. Check it: $37 + 73 = 110$. The units already make a ten, so the tens need only reach 9.
byKey.five-tens: From 40 to 100 is six tens, not five. Count them: 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100.

explain.text: You hopped 3 to reach 40, then jumped 60 to reach 100. The gap is $3 + 60 = 63$, so $100 - 37 = 63$.

screens.prose: Drag the point anywhere. The bar shows the gap up to 100, and the caption shows the pair that makes 100. Try 37, 58 and 81.
screens.question: Look at pairs such as 37 and 63. What do their digits add to?

options.text: The tens make 9 and the units make 10
The tens make 10 and the units make 10
options.why: That would total 110. The units already make a ten between them, so the tens need only 9.

options.text: The tens make 9 and the units make 9
options.why: That totals 99, one short of 100. The units must fill a whole ten.

hints.text: For 37 and 63, add the two tens digits, then the two units digits.

feedback.correct: Nine tens, and the units fill the tenth.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the tens digits of 37 and 63, then the units digits.

explain.text: 37 and 63: the tens give $3 + 6 = 9$, the units give $7 + 3 = 10$. That ten joins the nine tens to make 100. It works for every pair, except numbers ending in 0.

screens.prose: The partner is the **complement to 100**. Tens to 9, units to 10, unless the number ends in 0. The complement of 37 is 63.
screens.question: What is $100 - 58$?

hints.text: 5 needs 4 to make 9. 8 needs 2 to make 10.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the tens up to 9 and the units up to 10.

byKey.ten-each: You took both digits up to 10. $58 + 52$ is 110: the units' ten was counted twice.
byKey.nine-each: You took both digits up to 9. $58 + 41$ is 99, one short of 100.

explain.text: Tens: 5 needs 4 to reach 9. Units: 8 needs 2 to reach 10. So the complement is 42, and $58 + 42 = 100$.

screens.prose: Any subtraction is a gap. For $83 - 47$, start at 47 and count up to 83. Go to the next ten, then by tens, then the rest.
screens.question: What is $83 - 47$?

hints.text: How far is 47 from the next ten?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 47: to 50, to 80, to 83.

byKey.smaller: You took 3 from 7 in the units because 7 is bigger. But the 3 belongs to 83. Count up instead: 47, 50, 80, 83.
byKey.kept-ten: You borrowed a ten for $13 - 7$ but kept all 8 tens. Counting up never borrows.

explain.text: You counted up: 3 to 50, 30 to 80, 3 to 83. The gap is $3 + 30 + 3 = 36$. Check: $47 + 36 = 83$.

screens.prose: Counting up crosses 100 as easily as any other ten. The hop from 68 to 100 is just the complement of 68.
screens.question: What is $132 - 68$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 68 to 100, then on to 132.

byKey.smaller: You took the smaller digit from the larger in each column. Count up instead: 68, 100, 132.
byKey.kept-ten: You borrowed for the units but kept the tens whole. That leaves an extra ten.
byKey.no-hop: You counted from 70, not 68. The hop from 68 to 70 adds 2 more.

explain.text: You went 32 from 68 to 100, then 32 more to 132. The gap is $32 + 32 = 64$. Check: $68 + 64 = 132$.

screens.prose: When the two numbers are close, there may be no tens jump at all.
screens.question: What is $92 - 86$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 86 to 90, then to 92.

byKey.smaller: You took 2 from 6 because 6 is bigger. But the 2 belongs to 92. Count up: 86, 90, 92.
byKey.kept-ten: You borrowed for $12 - 6$ but kept the 9 tens whole. Count up: 86, 90, 92.

explain.text: You counted 4 up to 90 and 2 more to 92: the gap is 6. No tens jump was needed. That is the edge case: a gap smaller than 10 can still cross a ten.

screens.prose: Ben does $91 - 37$ the paper way, in his head. Units: 1 take 7 will not go, so borrow: $11 - 7 = 4$. Tens: $9 - 3 = 6$. He says 64.
screens.question: What is $91 - 37$?

options.why: That is Ben's answer. He borrowed a ten for $11 - 7$ but never took it from the 9 tens.
You took 1 from 7 because 7 is bigger. But the 1 belongs to 91, so the units need a borrow.
You took the borrowed ten off twice. The 9 tens become 8, and $8 - 3 = 5$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 37: to 40, to 90, to 91.

byKey.b: You borrowed in your head from right to left, and the borrowed ten slipped. Count up from 37 instead: 3, then 50, then 1.

explain.text: Borrowing in your head means holding a changed digit while you work on another, and that is where it slips. Counting up never borrows: 3 to 40, 50 to 90, 1 to 91. The gap is 54; check $37 + 54 = 91$.

screens.prose: Every gap today was found the same way: $$b - a = \text{hop to the next ten} + \text{tens} + \text{the rest}$$ For $100 - a$ this gives the complement: tens to 9, units to 10, unless $a$ ends in 0.
screens.question: For $74 - 28$, which hops do you count?

options.why: From 30, a jump of 50 lands on 80, past 74. The tens jump is 40, to 70.
You hopped by the units digit, 8. From 28 the next ten is 30, a hop of 2.

hints.text: Where is the next ten after 28?
28 to 30 is 2, 30 to 70 is 40, and 70 to 74 is 4.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Hop to 30, jump to 70, then go to 74.

explain.text: From 28: hop 2 to 30, jump 40 to 70, then 4 to 74. The gap is $2 + 40 + 4 = 46$, so $74 - 28 = 46$.

screens.prose: In an order book the **bid** is the best price a buyer offers. The **ask** is the best price a seller wants. The **spread** is the gap between them.

state.caption: The top row holds the best bid and the best ask

screens.question: What is the spread, in pence?

hints.text: Count up from the bid, £47.86, to the ask, £48.13.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from £47.86 to £48.13.

byKey.swapped: You took 13p from 86p. But 86p belongs to the lower price. Count up from £47.86 to £48.13 instead.
byKey.pound: You counted a whole pound from £47 to £48. The bid is £47.86, only 14p below £48.

explain.text: You counted up from £47.86: 14p to £48.00, then 13p to £48.13. The spread is 27p. Buying at the ask and selling straight back at the bid loses those 27p.

ideas: A subtraction is the gap between two numbers on the line.
Count up from the smaller number: hop to the next ten, jump by tens, then the rest.
The complement to 100 takes the tens to 9 and the units to 10, unless the number ends in 0.

formula.name: Subtraction as a gap
formula.tex: b - a = \text{hop to the next ten} + \text{tens} + \text{the rest}

summary.trap: Borrowing in your head from right to left, then losing the borrowed ten.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Tens to 9, units to 10.

byKey.ten-each: You took both digits up to 10. $64 + 46$ is 110.
byKey.nine-each: You took both digits up to 9. $64 + 35$ is 99.

explain.text: Tens: 6 needs 3 to make 9. Units: 4 needs 6 to make 10. So $100 - 64 = 36$.

quiz.prose: You pay for a £37.45 item with a £100 note. With pence, every digit goes up to 9 except the last, which goes up to 10. If the price ends in 0, the last non-zero digit goes up to 10 and the zeros stay.
quiz.question: How much change do you get?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take 3, 7 and 4 up to 9, and the last 5 up to 10.

byKey.ten-each: You took both pence digits up to 10. £37.45 + £62.65 is £100.10.
byKey.units-ten: You took the pounds' units digit up to 10. Only the very last digit goes to 10: £37.45 + £63.55 is £101.

explain.text: Digits to 9: 3 gives 6, 7 gives 2, 4 gives 5. The last digit, 5, goes to 10 and gives 5. The change is £62.55, and £37.45 + £62.55 = £100.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from 38: to 40, to 70, to 75.

byKey.smaller: You took 5 from 8 because 8 is bigger. But the 5 belongs to 75. Count up instead.
byKey.kept-ten: You borrowed for $15 - 8$ but kept all 7 tens. Count up instead.

quiz.prose: A stock is bid at £23.94 and offered at £24.11.
quiz.question: What is the spread, in pence?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count up from £23.94 to £24.11.

byKey.swapped: You took 11p from 94p. Count up from the lower price, £23.94, instead.
byKey.pound: You counted a whole pound from £23 to £24. The bid is only 6p below £24.

explain.text: From £23.94, 6p reaches £24.00 and 11p more reaches £24.11. The spread is 17p.
